The core innovation lies in defining a model-free conditional-association estimand Ψτ that captures how changes in exposure A affect the τ-th quantile of Y, without assuming a parametric quantile model. This is achieved by mapping the partially linear quantile model Qτ(Y|A,L) = βτA + ωτ(L) into an estimand that depends only on residuals (A − E[A|L]) and conditional quantiles. The efficient influence function is derived using the conditional quantile, exposure regression, conditional expectation, and density at the quantile. Cross-fitted DML and TMLE estimators are constructed to ensure honest inference, with convergence rates required to exceed n^-1/4. In practice, this leads to superior performance in finite samples compared to naive plug-in methods, especially in terms of bias and coverage. However, extreme quantiles pose challenges due to potential vanishing density, which necessitates conformalized fallback strategies to maintain stability.
